_comment: A deny-list scanned over what is about to leave the machine (docs/DESIGN.md §6).
A hit BLOCKS the push -- it does not warn. A leak is irreversible, and a
warning nobody reads is lesson #1 of this whole project.
Patterns are deliberately high-signal: shapes that are a credential or
nothing. A pattern that fires on ordinary config trains you to pass --force,
which is the same failure one step later.
`exceptions` are matched as plain substrings against the offending line, and
every one needs a reason. They are versioned so the next person can see what

patterns.reason: An unencrypted private key: SSH, TLS, PGP. Never belongs in a backup in the clear.
AWS access key id. The shape is unambiguous.
GitHub personal access / OAuth / refresh token.
OpenAI-style API key, including sk-proj- and sk-ant- variants.

A long literal assigned to something named like a credential. Quoted, 16+ chars, and not starting with $ or a backtick -- so a variable reference or command substitution reads as indirection, not as the secret itself.

exceptions.reason: A Chromium flag naming which keyring to use. Contains the word password, holds no secret.
A shell/editor option name, not a token.
age ciphertext is the intended way secrets are stored here (§6 allow-list), not a leak.
